correctness.rationale: Writing s=x+y+z and t=xy+yz+zx gives F=s^3-3st. Modulo 3 the target is s=1, with nine triples. For such s, s^3=1 modulo 9, so lifting to modulo 9 requires t=0 modulo 3. The number of nonzero coordinates is then 1 modulo 3, hence exactly one, with residue 1. In the class (1,0,0), substitution gives F(1+3a,3b,3c)-1=9[a+3(a^2+a^3+b^3+c^3-bc-3abc)]. The bracket is a modulo 3 and its a-derivative is 1 modulo 3: at precision 3^(k-2), each b,c pair has a unique root (vacuously for k=2), with three choices for the unused digit of a. This gives 3^(2k-1) points in each of three classes. Since every partial derivative of F is a multiple of 3, the linear Taylor increment by 3^k digits vanishes modulo 3^(k+1), and the higher terms vanish because 2k>=k+1. Thus each nonempty fiber has 27 elements and the count gives an image of size 3^(2k-1) at every k>=1.

The result describes both the point count and the compatible part of the solution tower, exposing the contrast between only one third of residues lifting and all 27 digits working when a residue does lift. This supplies the missing local data for the norm-one problem at its singular prime, not just a finite point count.
